newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan upbeat but concerned on stocks,inflation.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan upbeat but concerned on stocks,inflation.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan on Wednesday delivered an upbeat assessment of the U.S. economy but voiced concerns about skyrocketing stock prices and the risk of higher inflation.
"Even I must admit that our economic prospects in general are quite favorable," the central bank chief said in his semiannual Humphrey-Hawkins economic testimony to Congress.
But Greenspan warned that financial markets, including investors in stocks and junk bonds, may be over-optimistic about the economic outlook and urged caution.
"Such caution seems especially warranted with regard to the sharp rise in equity prices during the past two years," he said. "These gains have obviously raised questions of sustainability."
Greenspan credited much of the economy's recent good performance to the low rate of inflation, but said that may not last.
While inflation has remained quiescent, he saw what he called upside risks on the price front and made clear that the central bank was prepared to raise rates if needed to keep inflation down.
